_comment: Who speaks each line and how. Copy this file to your config folder (~/.config/orion-on-the-clock/ or
$ORION_CLOCK_CONFIG) and edit it there. Keys starting with an underscore are notes and are ignored.
host: the narrator. 'ref' is YOUR reference recording (a WAV of clear speech, about 10 to 20 seconds) on the
machine that runs the text to speech; '~' expands there. Clone only a voice whose owner has agreed to it.
'sha256_prefix' is the start (16 to 64 hex characters) of the recording's sha256: every real run checks it, so
a swapped file stops the run. Get it with: sha256sum host-reference.wav | cut -c1-16
'params' are Chatterbox's settings for every host line; 'params_cold_open' for the first, punchier line.
'post' is an ffmpeg audio chain applied after synthesis ('' for none).
Every other entry is an agent, keyed by the agent id your settings use (claude_code, codex, or an adapter's
harness). Every agent that appears in a day's ledger needs an entry here. An agent voice is Chatterbox's
built-in voice made distinct by its 'post' chain (it must start with asetrate=24000*); it never has a reference
recording. 'display', 'glyph' (up to 4 characters) and 'color' label it on the scoreboard and the confessional
card. 'active': false keeps its quotes off the air.
Changing this file after a day is voiced makes that day's render refuse (voice_config_changed) until it is
voiced again: the episode always matches the voices it was made with.
